name: FC Porto

head_coach.name: Francesco Farioli
style_keywords: possession and methodical build-up from the back
high, suffocating press on the opponent's first phase
counter-pressing to win the ball back immediately

identity.playing_style: Farioli restored a traditional 4-3-3 at Porto built on possession, patient construction from the goalkeeper (Diogo Costa) and a high, intense press that attacks the opponent's build-up; when possession is lost the team counter-presses rather than retreating. The structure is adjusted per opponent but the principles (possession, high press, territorial control) are constant. The 2025/26 title was won with the best-ever first-half record in an 18-team Portuguese league (49/51 points) and only 18 goals conceded in 34 games.
principles: develop-and-sell academy model (Mora, Martim Fernandes, Vasco Sousa, Prpic) with high release clauses (Mora EUR 70m, Alberto Costa EUR 65m, Borja Sainz EUR 100m)
financial restructuring under president Andre Villas-Boas after the Pinto da Costa era
coach-led tactical identity (Farioli contract extended to 2028)
continuity over churn: only three new signings for 2026/27 after a title season
revalidate domestic title while competing in the UCL
identity.club_character: Portugal's second-most decorated club and the historic northern counterweight to Lisbon's Benfica and Sporting; fiercely proud, demanding fanbase at the Estadio do Dragao with a strong 'us against the system' culture. Very high pressure on coaches; intense daily coverage from O Jogo, A Bola and Record. 2026 marks the club's return to the UCL after a season in the Europa League.
identity.ownership: Member-owned club (Futebol Clube do Porto) controlling FC Porto - Futebol, SAD (listed sports company). President Andre Villas-Boas, elected May 2024 with 79.96% of votes, ending Jorge Nuno Pinto da Costa's 42-year presidency; mandate 2024-2027.
identity.political_and_social_context: Publicly documented: Villas-Boas inherited roughly EUR 200m of supplier/lender arrears and total liabilities around EUR 513m, and had to liquidate old debts to satisfy UEFA's quarterly financial monitoring. The club suspended payments to an intermediary close to the former president over alleged fictitious services (Militao and Felipe sale commissions), a matter under criminal investigation by the Portuguese Public Ministry; the Court of Appeal sided with the club in Jan 2026.
identity.wage_structure: unknown (hierarchical in practice; Diogo Costa, Samu, Pepe at the top - figures not verified)
identity.transfer_policy: Buy young, high-ceiling profiles at moderate fees (Froholdt EUR 20m, Alberto Costa EUR 15m, Borja Sainz EUR 13.3m) with large release clauses; sell at peak (Eustaquio out 2026, Mora clause triggered but player refused Al-Ittihad); loans-with-option (Kiwior 2025) to spread cost
identity.injury_management_reputation: Samu missed the last three months of 2025/26 (injured from early Feb 2026) - the team still won the league; no wider public criticism of the medical department found.

last_season_2025_26.ucl_result: Not in UCL - UEFA Europa League quarter-final
last_season_2025_26.domestic_cup: Taca de Portugal semi-final (final won by Torreense over Sporting CP); Taca da Liga result not verified

squad.name: Samu Aghehowa
squad.injury_flag: missed Feb-May 2026 through injury; 2026/27 availability not verified

strengths: Best defence in Portugal in 2025/26: 18 goals conceded in 34 league games, built on Diogo Costa, Bednarek/Kiwior and a disciplined high press.
Clear, coach-driven identity (Farioli, contract to 2028) with continuity - only three summer arrivals and the core of the title side retained.
Young, appreciating assets with resale value: Froholdt (20, 50 apps/8 goals in 2025/26), Mora (19, EUR 70m clause), Alberto Costa, Prpic, Martim Fernandes.
Proven goal source in Samu (20 goals in 2025/26 despite missing Feb-May) plus Gabri Veiga's creativity (8 assists) and Pepe's experience.
Elite record in 2025/26 domestic play (28-4-2) and a Europa League quarter-final run give a competitive baseline for the UCL return.
weaknesses: Depth in central midfield after Eustaquio's sale: Varela, Froholdt, Hwang, Rosario and 19-21-year-olds carry a UCL + title-defence load.
Striker dependency: without Samu (injured from Feb 2026) the goals had to come from William Gomes and Froholdt (5 each); Andre Silva (30) is the only experienced back-up.
Financial constraints (EUR 500m+ liabilities, UEFA monitoring) limit wage growth and force sales when clauses are met.
Unproven at UCL level: several key players (Froholdt, Mora, Borja Sainz, Alberto Costa) have no Champions League experience.
Full-back depth thin on the left (Moura plus Zaidu only).

positional_needs.profile: box-to-box No.8 with UCL experience, 23-27, physical, secure under press
positional_needs.reason: Eustaquio sold to Swansea; midfield relies on 19-21-year-olds behind Varela.
Samu's three-month injury exposed the lack of a second reliable scorer; Andre Silva is 30 and a short-term fix.

positional_needs.profile: attacking left-back comfortable in a high line
positional_needs.reason: Only Moura and Zaidu; Kiwior can cover but is needed at CB.
